source.title: Do You Remember the Future? Weak-to-Strong Generalization in 3D Object Detection
source.authors: Alexander Gambashidze; Aleksandr Dadukin; Maksim Golyadkin; Maria Razzhivina; Ilya Makarov

page_placements.theme: Student-over-supervisor gains from input asymmetry (privileged or degraded views), and bias from supervisor-assisted reference labels

record.tranche_reason: Applies weak-to-strong distillation to LiDAR-based 3D object detection, an extension to vision, and reports detection results.
record.gate_note: The paper reports X-Ray model results against non-X-Ray baseline models. It does not report a matched weak-supervisor score for the student comparisons or calculate PGR, so these results do not directly test whether the student beats the weak supervisor or how PGR varies. The separately stated 79.5% and 59.2% mAP figures describe object-complete and original-frame models, not a matched student-versus-supervisor comparison; the 31.6% figure is an original model evaluated on object-complete data. Figure 3 is a qualitative comparison and is not included as a numeric result.
record.test_reason: Despite the title, this is privileged-information knowledge distillation, not weak-to-strong generalization. The teacher is trained on object-complete frames (79.5% vs 59.2% mAP on NuScenes), so it is the more accurate model in its own setting. The student is trained with ground-truth labels plus distillation losses. Every row compares the distilled student with the same architecture trained normally, which is the study's own method against its baseline. No weak-supervisor score on the student's inputs and no PGR are reported, so no version, V6 included, is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a teacher trained on object-complete frames gives accurate predictions and helps a plug-and-play student handle occluded and sparse objects. They claim the method improves all tested models. Table 1 contradicts this: the unscaled Waymo students score below their baselines. The authors call the teacher 'weaker', yet it is far more accurate in its own setting (79.5% vs 59.2% mAP).
record.recipe_differences: Uses temporal LiDAR object completion and a teacher-student distillation objective matching embeddings, regression and classification outputs, and features; it is not the original label-fine-tuning/PGR recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: On Waymo, the unscaled X-Ray models score below their listed baselines, whereas the scaled X-Ray models score above them. The authors state that they scale students on Waymo because object-complete frames are more informative there.

fits_no_version.finding: Distillation from a teacher trained on object-complete LiDAR frames, on top of ground-truth supervision, behaves differently by dataset and student size. On Waymo it raises scaled students' mAP slightly (+0.4 to +2.5) but lowers unscaled students' (-0.2 to -2.0). On NuScenes it adds about 1 mAP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge distillation from a privileged-information teacher improves LiDAR 3D detection over ground-truth-only training, depending on student capacity.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-24), Demonstrations Track
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are given. PGR and matched weak-teacher versus student scores are not reported. The paper's broad statement that the method improves tested models is not consistent with the table's unscaled Waymo X-Ray model scores, which are lower than their listed baselines.
record.rows_left_out: The Waymo table's plain baseline model rows are represented as baseline values rather than separate rows. The paired mAP/mAPH outcomes are all retained. The qualitative Figure 3 comparison and descriptive teacher/original-frame results are omitted because they do not provide a matched student-versus-weak-supervisor result.

untested.parts: No student-vs-weak-supervisor comparison and no PGR. The teacher is not weaker on its own inputs.
No confidence loss, ensembles or loss-variant comparison against naive weak-label training.
No PGR as a function of size or task.
The vision setting is labelled weak-to-strong, but there is no weak supervisor, student-beats-supervisor result or PGR.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and V6 labels are rejected. The weak-to-strong label is nominal: the student receives ground-truth labels plus distillation from a privileged, stronger-performing teacher. The teacher's score on the student's original-frame inputs is never reported, so no weak-supervisor baseline exists. This is a demo-track paper with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No matched quantitative comparison of the strong student with the weak teacher, and no PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensemble of weak supervisors, or comparison of loss variants.
The paper reports results across architectures and scaled models, but does not measure PGR or its dependence on supervisor/student size, task, or representations.
No tests of distribution shift, weak-supervisor blind spots, or correlated errors.
Tests LiDAR-based 3D object detection only; no other vision tasks or modalities.

relation.reason: Uses the weak-to-strong framing for teacher-student transfer with privileged object-complete inputs, without testing any catalog claim version through a student-versus-supervisor comparison.

tranche.reason: Applies a purported weak-to-strong distillation framework and reports its own method against baseline detectors. It does not establish that a student beats its weak supervisor or measure PGR.

source_check.notes: All checked rows are method-versus-baseline comparisons, not measurements of student improvement over a weak supervisor. The authors' universal improvement claim conflicts with unscaled Waymo results; the teacher's 79.5% and baseline's 59.2% mAP use different input conditions.

statements.correction: Supervised setting; annotated boxes and instance IDs used for object completion (§3.1); teacher-target distillation losses specified in §3.3. Waymo scaled-student mAP gains: SECOND L1/L2 +1.5/+2.5; CenterPoint +1.1/+1.0; DSVT Pillar +0.5/+0.4 percentage points. All unscaled Waymo students decline. NuScenes mAP: CBGS 50.0→50.8; CenterPoint-Voxel 53.4→54.3.
statements.problem: The numerical comparisons and dataset/size dependence are supported. An additional ground-truth supervision loss on top of distillation is not explicitly specified; supervised object completion uses ground-truth annotations.
